claude_code.supported_min_source: the .claude-plugin/marketplace.json schema this catalog ships has been stable since 2.0.0; the previous floor was never validated
claude_code.verification_method: Reviewed against the published changelog for 2.1.271 and 2.1.272; the CLI available on this run's runner already reports `2.1.273 (Claude Code)` — one release ahead of this catalog's reviewed 2.1.272 target — so it was used to re-run `claude plugin validate --strict --json .agents/skills` and `make validate` as a regression check (both passed clean), but is not itself evidence about 2.1.271/2.1.272-specific behavior; that review is changelog-based, continuing the precedent set for a `latest_known` bump reviewed from the published changelog rather than a live CLI at the exact target version (see the 2.1.258 entry in platform-targets.md). `validated_against` and `latest_known` both advance from 2.1.270 to **2.1.272** together (no divergence). **2.1.272** shipped only "bug fixes and reliability improvements" with no itemized entries — reviewed, nothing to adopt, matching the 2.1.226/…/2.1.263/2.1.264/2.1.266 fix-only precedent. **2.1.271** is the substantive delta reviewed here. One item is directly relevant and documented: **`--accept-command <sha256>` added to `claude plugin install` and `claude plugin update`** — lets a script accept exactly the command a previous `--json` run displayed, instead of the broader `-y`. Documented in the install guide's Useful-flags section alongside the existing 2.1.268 `--json` note, since a contributor scripting a catalog install smoke test can now pin acceptance to the specific reviewed command. Reviewed and found not applicable to this catalog, each checked directly rather than assumed: **enterprise `managed-mcp.json` parse-failure fix** (an unreadable/unparseable managed-mcp.json now keeps exclusive MCP control and warns at startup, instead of being silently ignored) — this personal catalog configures no `managed-mcp.json` and no managed MCP servers at all (checked via `grep` — the only existing `managed-mcp.json` mention in this repo's docs is the unrelated 2.1.259 `allowedMcpServers` scoping note), so neither the old silent-ignore bug nor the new warning behavior was ever exercised here; **`omitClaudeMd` agent frontmatter / `--agents` JSON field** — this catalog ships no custom or plugin subagents of its own, only the `run-plugins-catalog` contributor skill, so there is no agent frontmatter here for the new field to apply to; **per-command `allowed_domains` on Bash/PowerShell/Monitor in auto mode with sandboxing** — this catalog's own scripts (`scripts/*.sh`, `scripts/*.py`) run local checks only and declare no network-domain requirements, and this repo documents no Bash permission-rule examples for a consuming user to update either; **`modelPricing`/gateway `pricing` multiplier above 1** — no gateway or chargeback configuration exists for this personal catalog. Host/session/CI-side items with zero marketplace-manifest, plugin-source, or skill-loading surface, reviewed and confirmed out of scope: Remote/self-hosted-runner fast mode and `--drain-marker-file`, the `/config` panel mouse support, the org-policy-cache/tool-list-refresh fixes, the `ANTHROPIC_UNIX_SOCKET` proxy fix, cloud-session subagent schema-validation fix, `/fast` fixes, the long run of Bash-permission-check/`git`/sandbox fixes (none touch this repo's own permission-rule-free docs), MCP OAuth/tool-search/reconnect fixes, cross-session-message delivery notices, background-command double-start fix, `/model`/`/reload-skills`/`/resume`/`/teleport`/`--resume` fixes, artifact-watching and Markdown-artifact-rendering improvements (this catalog publishes no artifacts), terminal/rendering/spinner/hook-feedback polish, dynamic-workflow pause/resume, Claude in Chrome messaging, `claude mcp serve` progress pings, and the VSCode/Claude-Code-on-the-web/Claude-Tag/Code-Review/Windows-specific items. `claude plugin validate --strict --json .agents/skills` (piped through `scripts/report-skill-validation.py`) and a full `make validate` (regenerate + validate manifests, `make agent:check`, 3 plugins in sync, no drift) both passed clean, run against the 2.1.273 CLI available on this runner as a regression check for the catalog's own tooling — not a substitute for the changelog-based 2.1.271/2.1.272 review above.

cursor.supported_min_source: Cursor documents no minimum version for plugins; the floor is the version actually validated rather than guessed. The previous 0.45.0 floor predates Cursor's plugin system entirely
cursor.verification_method: latest desktop build from official Cursor download links (3.18.9, 2026-08-30 stable) cross-checked against cursor.com/changelog (feature 3.11; date-only entries through 2026-09-02 Self-Hosted Machines / Team Pools / partner sandboxes / computer use); team-marketplace import is a Dashboard flow

codex.supported_min_source: earliest release this catalog has claimed .agents/plugins/marketplace.json support for
codex.verification_method: documentary revalidation by this repo's standing Codex method (official release notes plus catalog compatibility review; the Codex CLI is not installed on the review machine). Reviewed every openai/codex release from 0.148.0 through 0.153.4 for plugin/marketplace changes: #41208 (0.151.0) reports invalid project marketplaces without hiding valid plugins, #41953 (0.153.0) enforces a marketplace source policy for OpenAI-curated plugins only, and #42149/#42150 (0.153.0) upgrade Git marketplaces from merged configuration and add remote-marketplace support to the plugin CLI. None alter the portable Agent Plugin catalog shape, so .agents/plugins/marketplace.json remains discoverable unchanged; 0.153.0 widens how it can be consumed rather than narrowing it.

opencode.supported_min_source: oldest version on which `skills.paths` discovery of a catalog plugin's skills was verified with `opencode debug skill`
opencode.verification_method: `opencode --version` on the maintainer machine (reported 1.18.29); latest from registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai. OpenCode has no marketplace, so the catalog itself cannot be installed — skill discovery is verified directly with `opencode debug skill`, pointing `skills.paths` at this repo's `.agents/skills` and confirming `run-plugins-catalog` resolves to its `SKILL.md`

capability_gaps.marketplace: OpenCode has no plugin marketplace and no plugin manifest, so this catalog cannot be added as an install source. Each plugin repo is installed directly — clone it and point `skills.paths` at its `skills/` directory, or symlink it into the OpenCode skills directory. Every plugin in this catalog ships its own `opencode.json` and its own OpenCode install guide.
capability_gaps.catalog_discovery: There is no OpenCode equivalent of listing plugins from a remote catalog. The plugin table in this repo's README is the discovery surface; installation is then per-repo.
